title: Applied ML Evals: End-to-End Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive, operational playbook for onboarding new models into Redwood's eval harness, creating and managing prompt sets and benchmarks, establishing quality guardrails, selecting and validating quantization profiles, and running a regression triage process to investigate and remediate quality regressions.
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a single, repeatable process for taking a candidate model from initial onboarding through continuous evaluation and safe production rollout, with concrete configs, SLOs, acceptance criteria, and an actionable regression triage flow. It exists to reduce time-to-serve while maintaining quality guardrails and clear rollback criteria.

Scope:
- Applies to all model variants intended for serving via Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers: eval harness configuration, prompt set creation and benchmarks, quantization profile selection and validation, automated quality checks, monitoring, and regression triage.
- Excludes model training procedures and proprietary dataset ingestion steps (handled by Research team).

Ownership and Roles:
- Model Owner: engineering (serving-runtime or applied-ml) — responsible for artifacts, baseline evaluation, and rollout plan.
- Eval Harness Owner: applied-ml team — responsible for CI/eval pipelines, metrics capture, and integration with monitoring.
- Quantization Owner: infer-optim team — provides quantization recipes and performance profiles.
- SRE/Observability: eng-platform/eng-sre — SLOs, alerts, and capacity planning integration.
- Stakeholder Reviewers: PM, Security (if restricted), Customer Success (if customer-facing).

SLOs and Acceptance Criteria (minimum):
- Quality: baseline automated eval pass rate >= 95% on canary prompt set (see "Prompt Sets" below). For language-model-specific metrics include: answer-coherence >= 0.92, hallucination-rate <= 0.04, instruction-following >= 0.90 (calculated by eval harness).
- Latency: median generation latency (50 tokens) < 150 ms for targeted VL-XS-1 SKU; p95 < 450 ms.
- Cost/Performance: tokens/sec improvement within expected range for quantized variants relative to baseline (see quantization profile table).
- Regression threshold: a drop in primary quality metric > 3% absolute or > 6% relative triggers regression triage.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. Prepare model artifacts:
   - Provide model package (weights, tokenizer, config) in Redwood model registry.
   - Include model card (README.md) with intended use, training data summary, license, and known failure modes.
2. Create baseline eval config:
   - Create an eval harness job under /eval-jobs/<model-name>/<version>/baseline with: dataset refs, prompt-sets, metrics config, and resource spec.
   - Example eval-harness config (JSON snippet):
     {
       "job_name": "baseline-eval",
       "model": "open-model-vX.1",
       "version": "vX.1-2026-05-12",
       "datasets": ["canary-prompt-set", "robustness-suite-v2"],
       "metrics": ["answer_coherence", "hallucination_rate", "instruction_following"],
       "target_slo": {"answer_coherence": 0.92}
     }
3. Define prompt-sets and benchmarks (see guidelines below).
4. Run baseline eval and record results in the eval dashboard.
5. Select quantization profiles to test: fp16 (baseline), q4_0, q4_1, int8 (where supported).
6. Run quantized builds through the same eval harness (end-to-end).
7. Review performance/quality tradeoffs with stakeholders.
8. Create canary rollout plan and automated monitoring/alerts.
9. Schedule regression alerting and daily digest for the first 72 hours of rollout.

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks - Guidelines:
- Canonical sets: define three canonical prompt sets per model: canary (100–300 examples, high signal, product-focused), robustness (edge cases, adversarial prompts, 500–1,000 examples), and micro-bench (fast checks, 20–50 examples for CI).
- Collection guidance: prompts should be grouped by intent, complexity, and token-length bucket (short < 32, medium 32–128, long >128).
- Metadata per prompt: id, intent_tag, expected_behavior (gold label or behavior description), difficulty, and author.
- Benchmark naming: <model-name>-<type>-v<year>-<sha>. Example: open-model-vX1-canary-2026-05-12.
- Evaluation metrics: for generative tasks use a combination of automated and human-evaluated signals (answer_coherence, factuality_score, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, instruction_following, safety_score).

Quantization profiles and validation:
- Profiles to consider: fp16 (no quant), q4_0 (4-bit symmetric), q4_1 (quantized with per-group scale), int8 (where hardware supports).
- Validation steps for each profile:
  1. Functional parity: run micro-bench prompt-set and ensure automated metric delta <= 2% for primary metrics.
  2. Robustness: run robustness suite; hallucination_rate must not increase by more than 0.03 absolute.
  3. Perf measurement: measure tokens/sec, median/p95 latency on target SKU. Must match perf expectations in profile catalog.
- Quantization profile manifest example (YAML-like inside string):
  profile_name: q4_1
  description: per-group scaling with activation-aware dequantization
  expected_quality_impact: -0.5% (answer_coherence)
  recommended_skus: [VL-XS-1, VL-S-2]
  validation_checks: [functional_parity, robustness_suite, perf_benchmark]

Quality guardrails (automated checks):
- Pre-deploy gate (CI): canary micro-bench must pass with defined thresholds (see SLOs). Failing CI blocks merge to model branch.
- Canary stage (10% traffic, 24–72 hours): daily eval-run, continuous monitoring of key metrics, automatic rollback on trigger.
- Production monitoring: periodic (hourly) eval jobs sampled from production traffic, safety filters, and drift detectors.
- Safety checks: flagged outputs with safety_score < 0.7 are logged and routed to safety review queue; any increase > 5x baseline triggers incident review.

Regression triage playbook (when an alert fires):
1. Triage intake (owner: model owner)
   - Record alert id, metric, magnitude, time window, and impacted routes.
   - Attach recent eval run artifacts and production sample outputs (redact PII).
2. Reproduce locally (owner: applied-ml)
   - Re-run the eval harness for the same model version and prompt set within CI environment.
   - If not reproducible, expand to adjacent prompt sets and recent traffic samples.
3. Classify root cause:
   - Categories: model regression (e.g., new weights), quantization-induced quality drop, infra/regression in runtime (KV cache bug), prompt-engineering/regression (changed templates), data drift.
4. Immediate mitigation:
   - If primary metric drop > 6% or safety regression present, initiate emergency rollback to prior stable version and scale down canary.
   - If quantization suspected, switch traffic to unquantized fp16 variant.
5. Postmortem and action plan (72-hour window):
   - Conduct working group with owners from serving, infer-optim, observability.
   - Deliver remediation plan (code fix, prompt adjustments, additional tests).
   - Schedule follow-up evals and blocked-release until tests pass.

Rollout and Canary Plan (recommended):
- Stage 0: Internal testing — CI and internal eval harness runs.
- Stage 1: Canary (10% traffic, 24–72 hours) — automated daily evals; change control required for extending duration.
- Stage 2: Ramp (10% -> 50% over 48–72 hours) — automated checkpoints at 10/25/50%.
- Stage 3: Full rollout (100%) — require two successive daily eval runs within SLO bounds.
- Rollout triggers and rollback criteria are codified in the rollout config stored in model registry.

Monitoring, Alerts, and Dashboards:
- Dashboards: per-model page in Redwood Console showing: baseline eval metrics, live canary vs production comparisons, latency distributions, safety trends, and token economics (tokens-in, tokens-out, cost/tokens).
- Alerts (examples):
  - Quality drop alert: primary_metric_drop > 3% over 6 hours — P1 to model owner and applied-ml.
  - Safety spike: safety_score < 0.7 occurrences > 5/hr — P0 to safety and SRE.
  - Latency breach: p95 > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes — P1 to SRE and serving-runtime.

CI and Automation best practices:
- All model submissions must include: eval-harness config, canary prompt-set, quantization-manifest, rollout-config, and test cases (micro-bench).
- Use ephemeral infra to run heavy evals; CI should prefer micro-bench for PR gating.
- Schedule full robustness and end-to-end evals nightly for active model branches.

Appendix: Helpful commands and snippets
- Run eval harness locally (CLI):
  redwood-eval run --job config/baseline-eval.json --model open-model-vX.1 --out results/baseline.json
- Promote model to canary (CLI):
  redwood-model promote --model open-model-vX.1 --version vX.1-2026-05-12 --traffic 0.10 --stage canary
- Example rollback (automated action):
  redwood-model rollback --model open-model-vX.1 --to-version vX.0-2026-04-02 --reason "auto-regression-trigger"

Appendix: Example evaluation matrix (describe table):
- Columns: metric, canary-threshold, production-threshold, action-if-breached
- Example rows: answer_coherence | >=0.92 | >=0.91 | trigger regression triage if breached; hallucination_rate | <=0.04 | <=0.05 | reduce rollout and open safety review
